source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use fluticasone only when acute wheezing begins, because inhaled corticosteroids are intended to provide rapid bronchodilation during an asthma attack.","B":"Swallow water immediately after each dose so medication remaining in the mouth is carried into the stomach and continues the anti-inflammatory effect.","C":"Rinse the mouth with water without swallowing after each inhaled dose to help reduce the risk of oropharyngeal candidiasis from local corticosteroid exposure.","D":"Avoid any valved holding chamber because spacers increase oral drug deposition and therefore increase the risk of candidiasis during inhaled corticosteroid treatment."}}
source_row.rationale: Current fluticasone HFA labeling instructs patients to rinse the mouth with water without swallowing after inhalation to reduce the risk of oropharyngeal candidiasis. Option C matches that instruction. Option A misuses a maintenance corticosteroid as a rescue bronchodilator. Option B tells the client to swallow rather than spit the rinse. Option D incorrectly discourages holding-chamber use.
source_row.source_detail: DailyMed Fluticasone Propionate HFA — Dosage and Administration §2.1 and Warnings/Precautions §5.1: rinse mouth with water without swallowing after inhalation to reduce oropharyngeal candidiasis; not indicated for acute bronchospasm. Current FDA fluticasone propionate HFA labeling at the cited DailyMed set ID; live version rechecked 2026-08-15.
